prerequisites: Basic formulation and nomenclature of organic and inorganic compounds.
Balancing chemical equations and simple stoichiometric calculations.
Ways of expressing solution concentration and associated stoichiometric calculations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to understand and apply the basic principles of general, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Consolidate knowledge of the fundamentals of chemical terminology, nomenclature, conventions and units.
Relate macroscopic properties with those of the atoms and molecules constituting matter.
Identify the characteristics of the different states of aggregation.
Describe the types of chemical reactions and their main associated characteristics.
Solve quantitative and qualitative problems according to previously developed models.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics and its applications in Chemistry.
Recognize and value chemical processes in daily life.
Relate Chemistry to other disciplines.
Develop critical reasoning.
Learn autonomously.
Acquire the ability to evaluate, interpret and synthesize chemical information.
Work in a team.
Demonstrate and fluently use basic knowledge of Chemistry.
Propose and solve basic problems in the field of Chemistry.
Correctly use the basic terminology employed in the field of chemistry, expressing ideas with precision, being able to establish relationships between different concepts.
Correctly apply the techniques used in a basic chemistry laboratory, including necessary calculations and expressing results appropriately.
Correctly prepare and present reports, both orally and in writing, corresponding to the laboratory practices carried out in the Chemistry course.

syllabus_topics: Object of Chemistry and its relationship with other sciences.
Meaning of chemical formulas and chemical nomenclature.
Formulation and nomenclature of simple inorganic and organic compounds.
Amount of substance, mole and Avogadro's number.
General properties of the states of matter.
Ways to express the concentration of solutions.
First principle of Thermodynamics: basic concepts.
Entropy and the second and third principles of Thermodynamics.
Control of reaction rate: influence of concentration and temperature.
Chemical equilibrium in a reaction between gases.
Control of chemical equilibrium and Le Châtelier's principle.
pH and dissociation constants of acids and bases.
Standard reduction potentials and electrochemical series.
Safety and Basic Operations in Laboratory
Toxicity of chemical substances. Pictograms and safety information sheets. Measurement of masses and volumes. Preparation of solutions.
Lewis structures. Determination of formal charges. Resonance.
Observation of reaction heats. Factors influencing reaction rate. Shifting chemical equilibrium. Chemical reactions in the separation and identification of ions.
Heat capacity and calorimeter constant. Determination of calorimetric curves.
Empirical kinetic laws. Initial rates method.
Volumetric determinations with chemical and/or instrumental indicator.
Reaction conditions. Product purification and yield determination.
Redox properties of metals. Measurement of the electromotive force of electrochemical cells.
Liquid-liquid extraction. Separation of binary mixtures.

assessment_methods.method: Classroom practices (PA) and Group tutorials (TG) work

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required in each assessed component (P1, P2, PA, TG, PL follow-up, PL written test). The weighted sum of the assessable aspects must be equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 to pass the course. If a student does not achieve a minimum of 4 in the first partial or does not take it, they will take a final exam (E Final) covering all topics, with a weighting of 60%. Mandatory attendance for all laboratory practices is required, except for justified absences.
